post.description:
Run the whole design of a project and tell how far it is on the way.

The answer is a stream of events. "progress" names the step and the fraction of the run, as often
as a step begins. The last event is "result", or "error" when the run failed. A project that cannot
be run at all is refused with 422 before the stream begins.

Without a system voltage the run stops after the shading: the result has the layout and the
shading, no options, nothing chosen, and no_options says what it waits for.

422.description: The request is refused. The message says why. An outline over 30,000 m² is refused with the code roof_too_large, before any work.

post.description:
A file of the design, for the option the project has chosen; the project file; or the zip of them all.

pdf: the report, A4 landscape. dxf: the layout, R2010 in metres, a layer for every string.
kmz: roof, obstacles and the modules in use, for Google Earth. csv: the 8,760 hours.
sld: the single-line diagram as a PNG. bom: the bill of materials as CSV. cables: the cable
schedule as CSV, a row a string. rtd: the project file, format 2: the request as the engine holds
it, and nothing of the design. zip: the seven files and the project file in one archive, each
entry named as its own download would be.

day: the reader's day (YYYY-MM-DD), printed on page 1 of the report; without it the server's
today. Every kind takes it; the report reads it, in the zip too.

For every kind but rtd the project must name its chosen option, and the design must have it.
rtd needs no chosen option, no system voltage, no weather and no run.

post.description:
Read a project file (.rtd) of format 1 or 2 with the engine's own reader.

The project comes back as a request carries it, in the current format. A file of format 1 names its
PAN, its OND and its CSV weather by path without their text: a note per file, in the engine's words,
says that the design asks for it again until it is chosen. A text that is not JSON, a JSON that is no
project and a format this version does not read are refused in words.
